story.iWant: to "heart" articles I find valuable with one click
story.soThat: I can show appreciation without creating an account

tasks.task: Create `layouts/_partials/widgets/heart-button.html` (project widgets convention; reconciles architecture's flat `_partials/heart-button.html` sketch). Wraps a `` with a Remix Icon `#heart-line` SVG-use, a `.heart-count` aria-live span seeded from `{{ index .Site.Data.umami_hearts .RelPermalink | default 0 }}`, and a `` `` JS-disabled fallback.

Mount the partial on article single pages in `layouts/single.html` `{{ else if eq .Page.Type "articles" }}` branch. Choose ONE: (a) sidebar info-widget (after the reading-time `` near line 119) — recommended, or (b) below-title inside `box-content` after the subtitle (line 62, before `{{ .Content }}`). Document choice in completion notes.

Investigate logs single-page rendering (run `hugo server`, visit a log URL, run `hugo --templateMetrics`). If logs DO render a single page → add a `Type == "logs"` branch to `single.html` mirroring the article branch and mount the partial there. If logs are card-only (PRD FR-027 "without detail pages") → add `{{ partial "widgets/heart-button" . }}` to the log card footer in `layouts/_partials/card.html` (after lines 148–161). Critical Agent Rule #2 forces card-footer placement only. Article mounting is non-negotiable; log mounting may be deferred to a follow-up if investigation reveals significant ambiguity — document and create issue.

Create `assets/js/hearts.js` — vanilla JS, IIFE wrapper, `'use strict';`. On DOMContentLoaded, query `.heart-button:not(.heart-button-fallback)`. For each button: (a) restore prior state from `localStorage['hearted-${articleUrl}']` (set `.hearted` class, `aria-pressed=true`, `disabled`); (b) on click — `try { window.umami?.track('heart', { article: articleUrl }) } catch` (non-fatal warn), optimistic `+1` on `.heart-count`, add `.hearted`, set `aria-pressed=true`, run heart-pop via `button.animate([scale1, scale1.3, scale1], { duration: 300, easing: 'ease-out' })`, persist localStorage, set `disabled=true`. Decide: stay-disabled (architecture canonical) vs. 1s re-enable (epics AC #7 literal) — both acceptable; document choice.

Bundle hearts.js into `layouts/baseof.html` footer slice (lines 25–34). Add `{{- $hearts := resources.Get "js/hearts.js" -}}` after `$header`, then include `$hearts` in the `slice` on line 33 so the order becomes `$sunCalc $main $search $firework $navbar $header $hearts`. Do NOT add a separate `` tag — keep single-bundle convention.

Create `assets/scss/elements/engagement.scss` with `.heart-button-wrapper`, `.heart-button`, `.heart-icon`, `.heart-count`, `.heart-button.hearted`, `.heart-button-fallback`. `@use "../vars/helpers"` and `@use "sass:color"` per existing pattern (mirror `elements/badge.scss`). Use Bulma variables / project gold-light helpers; ensure WCAG AA contrast for both default and `.hearted` states; include `:focus-visible` outline using `helpers.$gold-light`.

Register the new SCSS module in `assets/scss/main.scss` — add `@use "elements/engagement";` to the elements block (after `@use "elements/badge";` near line 38). Verify with `hugo --environment production` that `public/css/style..css` contains `.heart-button`.

CSP regression guard (no changes, verification only): re-read `config/_default/params.yaml` lines 25 (`scriptsrc`) and 29 (`connectsrc`); confirm both still contain `https://cloud.umami.is`. Build `hugo --environment production --minify` and grep `public/index.html` `Content-Security-Policy` `` tag for the same. (NOTE: production override at `config/production/params.yaml` may regress this — see C-CSP-PROD-OVERRIDE-INHERIT.)

Production build smoke: `hugo --environment production --minify` exits 0; no template-execution errors; no missing-resource warnings; no SCSS errors. Diff `public/articles/<an-existing-post>/index.html` before/after — only the new heart-button block differs. Existing card variants (`.is-horizontal`, `.is-log`, `.has-image`), info widget, TOC widget, series widget, related widget render unchanged.

Manual smoke (post-deploy on https://article-time.de/): heart button renders in chosen location; click triggers Umami POST 200 to `cloud.umami.is/api/send` with `{name:"heart",data:{article:"/articles/.../"}}`; animation plays; count increments; `aria-pressed=true`; `disabled` set; `localStorage['hearted-/articles/.../']=1`. Reload — pre-hearted state restored. DevTools Console / CSP clean. Cookies on `cloud.umami.is`: zero. Keyboard test: focus-visible outline, Space/Enter activates. No-JS test: `` fallback `` renders, count visible. Umami dashboard: `heart` event appears within ~30s.

Optional automation (only if Story 1.1's `tests/build/build-smoke.test.mjs` exists at implementation time — currently does NOT exist): add (1) HTML assertion that `public/articles/<post>/index.html` contains `class="heart-button"`, `data-article=`, and `aria-label=`; (2) bundle assertion that `public/js/footerBundle.*.js` contains the `'hearted-'` localStorage key prefix (proves hearts.js was bundled). Do NOT block on Story 1.1.

Inline documentation: header comment in `_partials/widgets/heart-button.html` — "Heart button — Story 2.2 (FR-008, FR-009). Reads count from data/umami_hearts.json (populated by Story 3.1). Click handler in assets/js/hearts.js fires Umami `heart` event."; header comment in `assets/js/hearts.js` documenting `window.umami` dependency (Story 2.1) and `hearted-${articleUrl}` localStorage key format. No separate doc page.

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: Heart button visible on every article single page (`Type == "articles"`) and every log entry — placement either sidebar info widget OR below the article title in `box-content`, dev's choice. Logs: dev determines current single-page layout for `Type == "logs"` and mounts in equivalent location, falling back to log card footer if logs have no detail page. (Epics AC #1; FR-008.)

Button shows current heart count sourced from `.Site.Data.umami_hearts` keyed by `.RelPermalink`. Hugo template: `{{ index .Site.Data.umami_hearts .RelPermalink | default 0 }}` with graceful fallback (file is missing until Story 3.1 lands; renders `0`). PRD's `.Params.hearts` sketch (03-core-features.md lines 266–268) is **superseded** by the architecture's `.Site.Data.umami_hearts` lookup (digital-garden-integration-architecture.md lines 296–308). (Epics AC #2; FR-009; ADR-002.)

Click triggers a Umami custom event `umami.track('heart', { article: button.dataset.article })`. The `umami` global is loaded by Story 2.1's snippet (head.html, production-only). In dev `umami` is undefined and the click is a silent no-op (acceptable). (Epics AC #3.)

Visual feedback: heart-pop scale animation `scale(1) → 1.3 → 1` over 300ms ease-out (Web Animations API or CSS keyframes — dev's choice). Brief textual confirmation via a `.hearted` state on the button (aria-live announcement "Hearted!" via the live region OR a transient `` that fades after ~1.5s). (Epics AC #4; architecture lines 458–462.)

Graceful degradation when JavaScript is disabled. Without JS, the button still renders (count is server-side rendered) and clicking does something meaningful — recommended `` fallback `♥ Share this article`. (Epics AC #5.)

Accessibility: native `` (Space/Enter activates by default); explicit `aria-label="Diesen Artikel mit einem Herz markieren"` (German is project default); `aria-pressed="false" → "true"` toggle; `disabled` after click; `aria-live="polite"` on the count or wrapping container; visible focus state via `:focus-visible`. (Epics AC #6.)

Click debounce: button is `disabled` for 1000ms after first click AND per-article hearted state is persisted in `localStorage` with key `hearted-${articleUrl}`. Combined effect: one heart per article per browser. **Decision flagged:** epics AC #7 says "debounce 1 second" while architecture pattern (lines 446–469) keeps the button disabled permanently — both satisfy AC #7; stay-disabled is architecturally consistent. (Epics AC #7.)

CSP regression check: this story does NOT modify CSP. Phase 0 Task 4.0 already added `https://cloud.umami.is` to `csp.scriptsrc` and `csp.connectsrc` in `config/_default/params.yaml` (lines 25, 29). After deploy: click a heart, DevTools Network shows POST to `cloud.umami.is/api/send` returns 200 with no CSP violation in Console.

Build still succeeds cleanly: `hugo --quiet --environment production --minify` exits 0 with no template errors, no missing-resource warnings, no SCSS compile errors. New partial, JS file, and SCSS file integrate without breaking existing build.

No regression to existing card / single-page layouts. Diff `public/articles/<existing-post>/index.html` before and after — only the new heart-button HTML block (and any sidebar restructuring needed to host it) should differ. Existing card variants (`.is-horizontal`, `.is-log`, `.has-image`), info widget, TOC widget, series widget, related widget render byte-equivalent. **Critical Agent Rule #1:** "NEVER modify existing card variants" — heart button is additive, never a replacement.

doc.title: Epics Breakdown
doc.snippet: Original 7 ACs verbatim. Story belongs to Epic 2 (Engagement Infrastructure), FR-008/FR-009 coverage, GitHub Issue #78. Effort: 2 days. Prereqs: Story 2.1 (Umami integration provides `window.umami`).

doc.title: Core Features (PRD)

JS sketch shows `umami.track('heart', { article: articleUrl })` + visual feedback. Daily fetch (Story 3.1) outputs `data/umami_hearts.json` keyed by RelPermalink.

doc.title: Functional Requirements
doc.section: FR-008 Anonymous Heart Button (lines 68–72), FR-009 Heart Count Display (lines 74–78), FR-010 Heart Count Persistence (lines 80–84)
doc.snippet: FR-008: readers can express appreciation with one click, no login. FR-009: heart count visible on cards and single pages, updates daily. FR-010: counts retrieved from analytics API and stored in data files (Story 3.1 owns).

doc.title: Technical Architecture Notes (PRD)
doc.snippet: Reference (not canonical) sketch: `` with `♥` and ``. JS uses `umami.track`, `button.classList.add('hearted')`, optimistic +1, `button.animate([...], { duration: 300, easing: 'ease-out' })`, `setTimeout(() => button.disabled = false, 1000)`. Superseded by digital-garden-integration-architecture lines 414–469 (canonical: localStorage persistence + IIFE).

doc.title: Integration Architecture
doc.section: Pattern 2: Dual Anonymous Engagement System — client-side hearts.js (lines 414–469); Hugo Data File Integration (lines 296–308); JS Module Pattern (lines 651–673); Critical Agent Rules (lines 762–771); Bundle size estimate (line 1106)
doc.snippet: Canonical hearts.js spec: `document.querySelectorAll('.heart-btn')`, localStorage `hearted-${articleUrl}` check, `window.umami` guard, optimistic UI, `button.disabled = true`. Data lookup: `{{ index .Site.Data.umami_hearts .RelPermalink | default 0 }}`. JS module: IIFE wrapper, 'use strict', DOMContentLoaded init. Critical rules: NEVER use jQuery, NEVER modify existing card variants, ALWAYS add new features to card footer, ALWAYS use `| default` on data lookups. Hearts.js sized ~1KB.

doc.title: Integration Architecture
doc.section: Security: Client-Side Considerations (lines 1056–1062); Edge Cases (lines 552–556); ADR-002 Popularity Scoring in Hugo Partial (lines 1309–1335)
doc.snippet: "LocalStorage for heart tracking: not secure, but acceptable for non-sensitive engagement data." Edge case: "Duplicate hearts: LocalStorage prevents (per-browser, not perfect but acceptable)." ADR-002: hearts read via `.Site.Data.umami_hearts` lookup in Hugo partials, not via Node.js scripts mutating frontmatter.

doc.title: Integration Architecture
doc.snippet: JS files: kebab-case (`hearts.js`, plural). SCSS files: kebab-case (`engagement.scss` — but story uses `elements/engagement.scss` per project convention; sibling files in `elements/` are flat). Data attributes: kebab-case (`data-article-id` per arch sketch — story uses `data-article` to match `architecture-notes.md` lines 102–108 short form). Project rule: scripts in root `scripts/`, partials by function (flat) — but project actually nests under `_partials/widgets/` for content widgets.

doc.title: System-Level Test Design
doc.snippet: Architecture is testable: static HTML inspectable, axe-core a11y check feasible via Playwright, Umami API mockable via msw/nock. For 2-day story scope: manual DevTools smoke (Network/Console/Application) + Umami dashboard verification + optional `tests/build/build-smoke.test.mjs` build assertions if Story 1.1 has landed.

In dev the global is undefined — heart click handler must guard with `if (window.umami) ...`. CSP precedent: `https://cloud.umami.is` already in `scriptsrc` + `connectsrc` (Phase 0 Task 4.0). package.name: Hugo Extended
package.version: 0.161.1 (CI pin in .github/workflows/daily-rebuild.yml line 50; minimum 0.115.0 in config/production/config.yaml)

hugo.package: Static site generator. Uses `hugo.IsProduction`, `resources.Get`, `resources.Concat`, `resources.Minify`, `resources.Fingerprint`, `index .Site.Data.X Y | default Z`, partial lookup. No version-specific features needed (heart-button uses long-stable APIs).
Required for `transpiler: dartsass` in head.html SCSS pipeline. Compiles `engagement.scss` and `main.scss`.
CSS framework — variables (`$text`, `$dark`, `$primary`, `$danger`), focus-visible defaults, Remix Icon integration. heart-button.scss uses Bulma `var(--bulma-text)` and helpers vars.
Used via `` pattern (matches other partials). `#heart-line` and `#heart-fill` are standard Remix icons.

node.package: CSS purging during production build. `.heart-button*` classes must survive purge (they appear in compiled HTML, so they will).
node.note: NO new npm dependencies. Hearts.js is vanilla; no webpack/rollup/esbuild step. Do NOT add `umami-cli`, `umami-tracker`, or wrapper packages — the official integration is the third-party tag from Story 2.1.

browser_apis.api: Browser global created by Story 2.1's tracker. Signature: `umami.track(name: string, data?: object) → void`. Called: `umami.track('heart', { article: button.dataset.article })`. Production-only; in dev the global is undefined and the click is a no-op.
Web Storage API. `localStorage.setItem('hearted-' + articleUrl, '1')` / `localStorage.getItem('hearted-' + articleUrl) === '1'`. Same-origin (CSP-irrelevant).

Web Animations API. `button.animate(keyframes, options) → Animation`. Used for the heart-pop scale animation. Feature-detect with `typeof button.animate === 'function'`; CSS keyframes is the alternative.
Standard DOM APIs. Init pattern: `if (document.readyState === 'loading') { document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', init); } else { init(); }`.

external_services.service: Anonymous, cookieless analytics. This story posts custom events via `umami.track('heart', { article })` — the call hits `https://cloud.umami.is/api/send` (already in `csp.connectsrc`). Daily aggregation (Story 3.1) reads stats via Bearer-auth `UMAMI_API_KEY` GitHub Secret (separate from the public website_id) and writes `data/umami_hearts.json` to the data-updates branch.

secret.name: UMAMI_API_KEY
secret.relation_to_this_story: DO NOT use in this story; not exposed to client

github_secrets.secret: Server-side bearer token for stats API; never rendered into HTML. Heart click on the client uses `umami.track` (no auth) which the third-party tracker script handles internally.

constraints.constraint: NEVER use jQuery in `hearts.js`. Vanilla JS only. (Critical Agent Rule #5; digital-garden-integration-architecture.md line 768.) Existing footer-bundle siblings (`main.js`, `navbar.js`, `header.js`, `search.js`) ARE jQuery-dependent legacy code — hearts.js coexists alongside them via IIFE + `'use strict';` isolation, NOT by participating in jQuery's `$(...)` chain.
Wrap `hearts.js` in IIFE `(function() { 'use strict'; ... })();`. Prevents global pollution; catches typos/implicit globals. (Architecture lines 651–673.)

If the heart button must be mounted on a log card (logs are card-only), it MUST go in the card footer (``), NOT on the card body, top, sides, or as an overlay. (Critical Agent Rule #2; architecture line 765.) Article-page mounting is exempt — sidebar widget OR below-title in `box-content` are both valid.

NEVER modify existing card variants (`.is-horizontal`, `.is-log`, `.has-image`, `.is-fixed`). Heart button is additive — a new partial, never a replacement. (Critical Agent Rule #1; architecture line 764.)

ALWAYS use `| default 0` on `index .Site.Data.umami_hearts .RelPermalink`. The data file does NOT exist yet (Story 3.1 creates it); without `| default`, the build will fail or render nothing once the data file is partially populated. (Critical Agent Rule #6; architecture line 769.)

Place the heart-button partial at `layouts/_partials/widgets/heart-button.html` (project widgets convention — siblings: `series.html`, `pagination.html`, `archive.html`). The architecture's flat `_partials/heart-button.html` sketch is reconciled in favour of the project convention. Either resolves via Hugo's partial lookup, but widgets/ is preferred.

This story does NOT modify CSP. Phase 0 Task 4.0 already added `https://cloud.umami.is` to `csp.scriptsrc` and `csp.connectsrc`. AC #8 is a regression check, not a change. Do NOT add new third-party domains.

Story 2.1 flagged that `config/production/params.yaml` redefines (replaces, not merges) `csp.scriptsrc` and `csp.connectsrc` and may NOT include `https://cloud.umami.is`. If 2.1 fixed it, hearts work. If 2.1 did NOT fix it, the heart button will visually render but Umami POSTs from `umami.track` will be CSP-blocked in production — symptoms: console "Refused to connect to https://cloud.umami.is/api/send" + zero hearts in the Umami dashboard. AC #8 (CSP regression) catches this only post-deploy. If observed during smoke test, escalate to SM and fix the production override (NOT in this story; that's 2.1's responsibility).

The `window.umami` global is loaded ONLY in production (Story 2.1 gates the `` with `{{ if hugo.IsProduction }}`). hearts.js MUST guard with `if (window.umami) ...` so the click is a silent no-op in dev. Do NOT add a `hugo.IsProduction` gate around the heart-button partial itself — the button must render in dev (so it's testable); only the tracking call short-circuits.

LocalStorage `hearted-${articleUrl}` is per-browser, clearable, and incognito-bypassable. This is acceptable: hearts are an engagement signal, not a vote. Anti-abuse / rate-limiting is out of scope (Umami Cloud dashboard rules can mitigate post-launch). (Architecture lines 1056–1062.)

Epics AC #7 says "debounce 1 second" via `setTimeout(() => button.disabled = false, 1000)`. Architecture pattern (lines 446–469) keeps the button permanently disabled (localStorage check on next page load). Stay-disabled is the architecturally consistent choice and satisfies AC #7's "prevents double-clicks within 1 second" trivially. Either is acceptable — document the choice in completion notes.

`layouts/single.html` has branches for `Type == "page"` (lines 2–32) and `Type == "articles"` (lines 34–216) but NO branch for `Type == "logs"`. Yet `content/logs/log-test-2/` exists. PRD FR-027 says logs are "without detail pages" — three interpretations: (1) logs are card-only — heart on card footer; (2) logs render via fallback `single.html` and need a logs branch added; (3) logs are leftover scaffolding to delete. Investigate first via `hugo server`, then decide. Article-page mounting is non-negotiable; log mounting may be deferred to a follow-up if investigation reveals significant ambiguity.

Hugo v0.146+ flat layouts convention — DO NOT create `layouts/_default/baseof.html` or `layouts/_default/single.html`. The project uses `layouts/baseof.html` and `layouts/single.html` at root. (Same constraint as Story 2.1.)

Bundle hearts.js into `footerBundle.js` (existing single bundle in `baseof.html` lines 25–34). Do NOT add a separate `` tag. Bundle bloat is negligible (~1KB) and fingerprinting handles cache-busting automatically.

The footer bundle is loaded with `` (baseof.html line 34). hearts.js inherits this — it does NOT need its own script tag. The IIFE init waits for `DOMContentLoaded` (via the readyState check), so race conditions with the deferred load are handled.

Button text vs background contrast must meet WCAG AA (4.5:1) for both default and `.hearted` states. Verify with WebAIM Contrast Checker or axe-core. Project has only the dark theme (`data-theme="dark"` on `` in baseof.html line 2) — no light-theme styling needed.

Active element is `` — performs an action, not navigation. The `` fallback is `` because without JS the action degrades to a navigation link. `type="button"` is critical to avoid implicit submit if ever placed in a ``.

Use `aria-pressed="false"` on initial render, toggle to `"true"` on heart. Use `aria-live="polite"` on the count `` (or wrapping container) so screen readers announce the +1. Use a clear `aria-label` (German: "Diesen Artikel mit einem Herz markieren" — project default).
Visible focus state via `:focus-visible` (not `:focus`, which can over-fire on mouse). Use Bulma's existing focus styles or augment with `helpers.$gold-light` outline.
No new npm dependencies. The Web Animations API + localStorage are browser-native; no polyfills needed (Story targets modern evergreen browsers).

Use `data-article="{{ .RelPermalink }}"` (not `data-article-id` or `data-permalink`). Architecture-notes.md sketch uses `data-article`; integration-architecture sketch uses `data-article-id`. Reconciled to `data-article` — hearts.js reads `button.dataset.article`.
Use Hugo whitespace controls (`{{- ... -}}`) on the surrounding template lines for clean diff and minimal whitespace in rendered HTML. (Same project convention as other partials.)

aria-label and any user-visible text default to German (project convention — existing strings: "Weiterlesen", "Zurück zum Seitenanfang", "Veröffentlichungsdatum"). No `i18n/` translation files are in use; if a future bilingual pass occurs, the partial can be revisited.
Do NOT edit `content/pages/datenschutz.md`. Story 2.5 (Privacy Policy Page) explicitly owns the hearts privacy disclosure text.
Do NOT add a `hearts:` frontmatter field to articles. Heart counts are data-file-driven (`data/umami_hearts.json` via Story 3.1), NOT per-article frontmatter. (ADR-002 + ADR-001.)

interface.name: .Site.Data.umami_hearts
interface.kind: Hugo data (read; JSON file in data/ directory, populated by Story 3.1)
interface.signature: {{ index .Site.Data.umami_hearts .RelPermalink | default 0 }} → integer (heart count for this page; 0 if data file or key missing)
interface.path: data/umami_hearts.json (FUTURE — does not exist yet; Story 3.1 creates it). Consumed in layouts/_partials/widgets/heart-button.html.

interface.name: .RelPermalink
interface.signature: {{ .RelPermalink }} → string (e.g., "/articles/my-post/") with trailing slash; used as both data-article attribute value and data-file lookup key

interface.name: partial "widgets/heart-button"
interface.signature: {{ partial "widgets/heart-button" . }} → renders heart button HTML (button + count + noscript fallback). Context (`.`) is the article/log Page object — uses `.RelPermalink` and `.Site.Data.umami_hearts`.
interface.path: layouts/_partials/widgets/heart-button.html (NEW). Mounted from layouts/single.html (articles branch) and conditionally layouts/_partials/card.html (log card footer).

interface.name: window.umami.track
interface.kind: Browser global (third-party — provided by Umami tracker script loaded by Story 2.1; ABSENT in dev and when JS disabled)
interface.signature: umami.track(eventName: string, eventData?: object) → void (fire-and-forget; no return; sends XHR POST to https://cloud.umami.is/api/send). Story 2.2 calls: umami.track('heart', { article: button.dataset.article }).
interface.path: (browser global, runtime-injected). Created when the Umami tracker script (loaded by Story 2.1's snippet in head.html, gated by hugo.IsProduction) finishes loading.

interface.name: localStorage (Web Storage API)
interface.kind: Browser API (read/write; same-origin, persistent across reloads)
interface.signature: localStorage.getItem('hearted-' + articleUrl) → string|null; localStorage.setItem('hearted-' + articleUrl, '1') → void. Key format: `hearted-${articleUrl}` (e.g., `hearted-/articles/my-post/`).

interface.name: HTMLButtonElement.animate (Web Animations API)
interface.signature: button.animate(keyframes: object[], options: { duration: number, easing: string }) → Animation. Story 2.2 uses keyframes [{transform:'scale(1)'},{transform:'scale(1.3)'},{transform:'scale(1)'}] with duration 300, easing 'ease-out'. Feature-detect via `typeof button.animate === 'function'`; CSS @keyframes is the alternative.
interface.path: (browser DOM; widely supported in evergreen browsers since 2016)

interface.name: resources.Get / resources.Concat / resources.Minify / resources.Fingerprint
interface.kind: Hugo asset pipeline functions (used in baseof.html footer bundle)
interface.signature: resources.Get "js/hearts.js" → Resource; slice $sunCalc $main $search $firework $navbar $header $hearts | resources.Concat "js/footerBundle.js" | resources.Minify | resources.Fingerprint → Resource (fingerprinted JS bundle)
interface.path: layouts/baseof.html lines 25–34. Existing pattern; story extends slice.

interface.name: hugo.IsProduction
interface.kind: Hugo built-in function (read, boolean) — INHERITED dependency only
interface.signature: {{ if hugo.IsProduction }} → true when invoked with --environment production; false in hugo server default. Story 2.2 does NOT use this directly — but Story 2.1 uses it to gate the Umami script load, which is why hearts.js must defensively guard `if (window.umami)`.

tests.standards: Manual smoke is the primary test strategy for this 2-day story (matching the lightweight pattern Story 2.1 established for Epic 2). Per `docs/2-solutioning/test-design-system.md` and the test-layering precedent established by Story 1.1 (`tests/build/` via node:test, `tests/e2e/` via Playwright, optional axe-core for a11y), heart button has a small browser-only behavior surface that is most efficiently tested via DevTools (Network/Console/Application/LocalStorage/Cookies tabs) plus the live Umami Cloud dashboard. `tests/` does NOT exist yet — Story 1.1 bootstraps it; if 1.1 lands first, two ~10-line node:test build assertions can be added. Otherwise rely on manual smoke. `axe-core` checks (via Playwright) are a stretch goal; manual NVDA / VoiceOver pass on at least one article page is the minimum a11y verification. ALWAYS use `| default 0` when accessing `.Site.Data.umami_hearts` (Critical Agent Rule #6 — non-negotiable). NO unit tests for hearts.js — DOM-bound code with browser-only dependencies; integration testing in a real browser is more valuable than mocked unit tests for this scope. Test failures of "Umami event not received" must NOT block merge if Console shows a successful POST and CSP is clean — the dashboard ingestion is asynchronous (~30s) and outside the project's control.

ideas.idea: Manual: visit `https://article-time.de/articles//` in fresh incognito. Confirm heart button visible in chosen mounting location (sidebar widget — recommended — OR below title in `box-content`). Verify the button's count text matches `0` (until Story 3.1 lands and populates `data/umami_hearts.json`).

Manual: visit a log entry (e.g., `https://article-time.de/logs/log-testing/`). If logs render a single page → confirm heart button on that page. If logs are card-only → confirm heart button in the log card footer on the logs listing page (`https://article-time.de/logs/`).

Build assertion (optional, if `tests/build/build-smoke.test.mjs` exists): grep `public/articles//index.html` for `class="heart-button"` AND `data-article="/articles/`. Confirms the partial rendered with the data-file-driven count (default 0 until Story 3.1).

Manual DevTools: click heart button, switch to Network tab, filter by `umami`. Assert exactly one POST to `cloud.umami.is/api/send` returns 200. Inspect request body: `{"name":"heart","data":{"article":"/articles//"}}`. No CSP violation in Console.

Manual DevTools: confirm `umami` Console: `typeof window.umami` → `'object'` in production, `'undefined'` on `hugo server`. Confirms Story 2.1's prod-gate works and hearts.js's `if (window.umami)` guard is necessary.
Manual DevTools: click heart, observe heart-pop scale animation (1 → 1.3 → 1 over 300ms ease-out). Use DevTools Performance tab → Record → Click → Stop, look for the animation frame.
Manual DevTools: after click, confirm the count `` increments by 1 immediately (optimistic UI). The aria-live region announces the new count.
Manual: DevTools → Settings → Disable JavaScript → reload article page. Confirm `` fallback `` renders, count visible (server-rendered via Hugo data lookup), link works (jumps to fragment).

Manual keyboard test: Tab to heart button → focus-visible outline appears (gold-light per SCSS) → press Space → heart activates, count increments, button disables, aria-pressed flips to `true`. Press Tab away and back — focus state still correct (button stays disabled per stay-disabled choice OR re-enables after 1s per debounce choice).

Manual screen-reader test (NVDA or VoiceOver): navigate to heart button. Announcement before click: "Diesen Artikel mit einem Herz markieren, button, not pressed". After click: "Hearted!" (live region) and "pressed, dimmed" via aria-pressed=true + disabled.
Optional automation (if Playwright + axe-core land): run `axe.run('article')` on an article page; assert 0 violations on the heart button. Defer to Epic 9 if not landed.

Manual DevTools: Application → Local Storage → `https://article-time.de` → after click, confirm key `hearted-/articles//` with value `1`. Reload page → confirm button is rendered already-hearted (count includes the +1, button disabled, aria-pressed=true).
Manual DevTools: rapid double-click within 1 second on a fresh article (clear localStorage first). Confirm only ONE POST to `cloud.umami.is/api/send` (button disabled after first click).

Manual / scripted: build with `hugo --environment production --minify`, grep `public/index.html` for `Content-Security-Policy` `` tag — assert `script-src` and `connect-src` both contain `https://cloud.umami.is`. Catches C-CSP-PROD-OVERRIDE-INHERIT regression from Story 2.1.
Manual DevTools: Application → Cookies → both `article-time.de` and `cloud.umami.is` — assert zero cookies set by either origin. (Same regression check as Story 2.1's AC #4.)

CI / local: run `hugo --environment production --minify` and assert exit 0, no stderr WARNINGS, no template errors. Existing `daily-rebuild.yml` workflow's "Build Hugo site" step (line 122) provides automated coverage post-merge.

Manual / scripted: build `public/` before and after the change; diff `public/articles//index.html`. Only the new heart-button HTML block (and any sidebar restructuring needed to host it) should differ. Existing card variants, info widget, TOC widget, series widget, related widget render byte-equivalent.

Build assertion (optional, if `tests/build/build-smoke.test.mjs` exists): glob `public/js/footerBundle.*.js`, read content, assert it matches `/hearted-/` (the localStorage key prefix in hearts.js). Proves the file was bundled.

Manual: visit article in incognito, click heart, close incognito, reopen incognito on same article. Confirm: localStorage is fresh (count is back to `0` + 1 = 1 after click), Umami logs the event again. (Confirms localStorage is per-browser-session in incognito, not persistent — acceptable per C-LOCALSTORAGE-NOT-SECURE.)

Manual: within ~30 seconds of clicking, log into `https://cloud.umami.is` → select website → Events tab → confirm a `heart` event appears with `article: /articles//` data. Verifies end-to-end ingestion (depends on Umami Cloud's async pipeline; not blocking on dashboard latency).
